headline: President Bush set up an emergency board to look into a labor dispute between SEPTA and its train conductors' union.
what_it_does: This order creates an emergency board to investigate a dispute between the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority (SEPTA) and its conductors, who are represented by the United Transportation Union. Under federal railway labor law, boards like this usually study the dispute and make recommendations, and a strike or lockout is generally put on hold while the process plays out. The title does not give details about what the dispute involves.

who_it_affects.group: SEPTA train conductors in the United Transportation Union
who_it_affects.how: Their labor dispute with SEPTA is reviewed by a federal emergency board, which typically delays any strike while the review happens.
The agency's dispute with its conductors goes before a federal board, which generally means it cannot change working conditions or lock out workers during the review.

who_it_affects.group: Commuter rail riders in the Philadelphia region
who_it_affects.how: Rail service is likely to keep running while the board does its work, since a strike is usually put off during this process.
